topic: Law change: Delhi (Right of Citizens to Time-Bound and Easy Delivery of Services) Act, 2026 notified, replacing the 2011 law - statutory right to notified Delhi government services within fixed time; designated officer per service; online applications with unique tracking number; delay fine on officer Rs 250/day up to Rs 5,000; wrongful rejection Rs 250-5,000; officer heard before penalty; delayed application becomes automatic appeal to Citizen Grievance Redressal Authority (30 days), then Delhi Right to Service Commission; covered services and deadlines to be notified (announced 9 Nov 2026)

slides.title: Late government service? Officer pays **Rs 250 a day**
slides.subtitle: Delhi's new law gives citizens a **legal right** to get notified government services within a **fixed time**.
slides.cite: **Delhi (Right of Citizens to Time-Bound and Easy Delivery of Services) Act, 2026** · notification announced **9 Nov 2026**

slides.label: What has changed
slides.title: A new law replaces the **2011 Act**
bullets: Getting a covered service on time is now a **statutory right**, not a favour.
The government will notify **which services** are covered, the **maximum days** for each, and the **officer responsible**.
It applies to Delhi government departments, **local bodies** and notified institutions.

slides.label: How it works
slides.title: Apply online, **track** every step
bullets: You can apply **online** and get a **unique application number** to check the status.
The time limit starts once your **complete application** is received.
If your application is rejected, the officer must give the **reason in writing**.

slides.label: Penalties
slides.title: Fines on **careless officers**
bullets: Unjustified delay: **Rs 250 per day**, up to a maximum of **Rs 5,000**.
Rejecting an application without good reason: a fine of **Rs 250 to Rs 5,000**.
The officer gets a chance to **explain** before any fine is imposed.
slides.note: **Law fact:** the fine is recovered from the officer's salary and goes to the **government treasury**. It is not paid to the applicant.

slides.label: Deadline missed?
slides.title: Your application becomes an **appeal**
bullets: You do **not** need to file a fresh appeal. A delayed application is **automatically** treated as an appeal to the **Citizen Grievance Redressal Authority**, which normally decides in **30 days**.
If it is still not resolved, the matter goes to the **Delhi Right to Service Commission**.

caption:
Waiting endlessly at a government office in Delhi? A new law now puts a price on delay ⏱️⚖️

The Delhi government has notified the Delhi (Right of Citizens to Time-Bound and Easy Delivery of Services) Act, 2026, which replaces the 2011 law. It gives citizens a statutory right to get covered government services within a fixed time. The government will notify which services are covered, the maximum number of days for each, and the officer responsible. It applies to Delhi government departments, local bodies and notified institutions.

You can apply online and track your application with a unique number. If it is rejected, the reason must be given in writing. An officer who delays without justification can be fined Rs 250 per day, up to Rs 5,000, and wrongful rejection can attract a fine of Rs 250 to Rs 5,000. The officer must be heard before any fine. Keep in mind: the fine goes to the government treasury, not to the applicant.

If the deadline is missed, you don't need to file a fresh appeal. Your application is automatically treated as an appeal to the Citizen Grievance Redressal Authority, which normally decides within 30 days. Unresolved matters go to the Delhi Right to Service Commission. Watch for the official list of covered services and timelines.

Law: Delhi (Right of Citizens to Time-Bound and Easy Delivery of Services) Act, 2026 (notification announced 9 Nov 2026)

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
